Ad Skipper

Presses YouTube\'s "Skip Ad" button for you, so that watching does not require reaching the screen every few minutes — for people with limited hand movement, people recovering in bed, and anyone whose hands are occupied or out of range when an ad starts. Ads with no Skip button cannot be shortened by anything outside YouTube, so it silences those instead. It watches YouTube and its picture-in-picture window only, reads screen content from YouTube only, and the sole action it performs is pressing that one control.
Ad audio
Silence ads while they play

Mutes the media volume while an ad is on screen and unmutes it as the ad ends — the only thing that helps with ads that have no Skip button. It needs no extra permission, never touches your ringer, notifications or alarms, and a volume key always overrides it. If something kills the app mid-ad, the sound is restored the next time the service starts.
Overlay ads
Dismiss the "Sponsored" card over the video

The small card that slides over the bottom of the player after an ad has no close button — only a ⋮ that opens a menu with Dismiss in it. This opens that menu and taps Dismiss for you. It only ever touches the ⋮ belonging to that card, never the advert itself, and it will not tap anything in the menu until the menu has identified itself as the ad menu. If it cannot find what it expects, it does nothing.

How do I lock it in Recents?
Locking an app in Recents

1. Open Recents — swipe up and hold, or tap the square button.
2. Pull down on the Ad Skipper card, or press and hold it.
3. Tap the padlock.

A locked app is skipped when you clear all apps, which is what keeps the service alive.

This is a general illustration. The control differs between devices — some use a padlock, some a pin, some a menu item called Lock. If your Recents screen has none of them, this device probably does not close apps that way.
Diagram of a Recents screen with the middle app card pulled down to show a padlock

Android is not letting it read the screen, so no ads will be skipped. Turn Ad Skipper off and back on in Accessibility settings. If it keeps happening, allow the app to run in the background without restriction. Tap here to open the app.
Ad Skipper is NOT CONFIGURED
The service is running, but the setup checks have not been completed, so it will stop working without warning. Tap here to finish setup.

1. Lock it in Recents. Open Recents, pull down or long-press the Ad Skipper card, and tap the padlock. On devices where "clear all apps" is a force stop, this is the only thing that survives it.

2. Allow auto-start, if this device has such a list. Without it the system may refuse to restart the service after anything closes it, leaving it enabled but dead.

On stock Android neither is needed; the system restarts the service by itself.
